newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fijian ship rescues 25 adrift in South Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Fijian ship rescues 25 adrift in South Pacific.

text.p: A Fijian ship on Monday rescued 25 passengers who had drifted for 30 hours in liferafts after their ship caught fire in the South Pacific, rescue officials said.

New Zealand rescue coordinators said the 25 passengers and crew of the MV Avatapu, including three children, were safely transferred to the Fiji-registered cargo ship Pacific Explorer in the early hours of Monday.
"They were still all happy, well and in good spirits," said Flight Lieutenant Jeoff (repeat Jeoff) Barraclough of the New Zealand Air Force's Rescue Coordination Centre.
He said the Pacific Explorer was on its way to Rarotonga in the Cook Islands and should arrive late on Tuesday.

An engine-room fire forced the MV Avatapu's 25 passengers to abandon the 250-tonne interisland trading ship on Saturday evening, while sailing in the Cook Islands group. No one was killed in the fire.

Some 200 nautical miles from the nearest land, the passengers took to the lifeboats and sent a distress beacon which was picked up by satellite and spotted by a commercial aircraft flying over the region.
A New Zealand air force Orion aircraft was despatched from Auckland, and early on Sunday dropped food, medical supplies and a radio transmitter to the survivors.

Barraclough said a second Orion arrived at the scene around midnight on Sunday and acted as a homing signal for two ships, the Pacific Explorer and the Russian container vessel Anadyr, which were diverted to the scene.
"After that it was all fairly standard. They transferred the passengers onto the Pacific Explorer, and even recovered the liferafts," he said. He could not confirm the nationality of the passengers.
After the rescue, the abandoned vessel was left afloat and on fire.
